# Issue #41: `slugify` produces double hyphens and trailing hyphens

`slugify("Hello,  World!")` returns `"hello--world-"` but should return `"hello-world"`.
Also `slugify("--a--b--")` should give `"a-b"`.

Please fix `textkit/slug.py`. Do not change the public signature.


Repository files:
tests/test_slug.py
textkit/__init__.py
textkit/slug.py

1| import re

   3| def slugify(text: str) -> str:
   4|     """Turn arbitrary text into a URL slug: lowercase, ASCII letters and
   5|     digits, words separated by single hyphens, no leading/trailing hyphens."""
   6|     text = text.lower()
   7|     text = re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]", "-", text)

The bug is clear: the regex replaces every non-alphanumeric character with a hyphen but never collapses runs of hyphens or strips leading/trailing ones. Minimal fix:

arguments.old:
text = text.lower()
    text = re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]", "-", text)
    return text

arguments.command: python -c "from textkit import slugify; print(repr(slugify('Hello,  World!'))); print(repr(slugify('--a--b--'))); print(repr(slugify('Hello World')))"

content: Both issue examples now produce the expected output (`"hello-world"` and `"a-b"`), and the test suite passes. The fix was minimal: the character class now matches runs of non-alphanumeric characters (`+`), collapsing them into a single hyphen, and `strip("-")` removes any leading/trailing hyphens. The public signature is unchanged.

arguments.summary: Fixed slugify in textkit/slug.py by changing the regex from `[^a-z0-9]` to `[^a-z0-9]+` so consecutive non-alphanumeric characters collapse into a single hyphen, and added `.strip("-")` to remove leading/trailing hyphens. This makes slugify("Hello,  World!") return "hello-world" and slugify("--a--b--") return "a-b", as required by issue #41. The public signature is unchanged and the existing test suite passes.
